newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean plantings 96 percent done - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean plantings 96 percent done - Safras.

text.p: Brazilian soybean plantings were 96 percent completed by December 19 against 90 percent by December 21, 1995, and an average of the past five years of 95 percent, consultants Safras e Mercado said.
Plantings by December 12 this year were 92 percent.

A drop in rainfall last week allowed good progress in plantings and these should be rapidly completed, although many producers were still hoping for fresh heavy rains to ensure the plants developed at a consistent pace.

Growers said the climate was favorable in most areas but plantings were lower than formerly expected in some regions like Rio Grande do Sul and Sao Paulo, where farmers were having trouble obtaining credit.
Last year a drought hit Rio Grande do Sul in particular, delaying plantings to the extent that 30 percent of sowings in the state were only done after Christmas.
Plantings of the 1996/97 crop by December 19 per state as estimated by Safras are as follows in percentage terms.
RIO GRANDE DO SUL - lack of credit means planted area is lower than earlier estimated. Climate satisfactory but must be maintained to guarantee harvest meets forecast of 5.7 million tonnes.
PARANA - situation very favorable to state meeting record harvest prediction of 6.7 million tonnes.

MATO GROSSO - growers say one rainfall per week needed to make sure plants develop homogenously. Early planting in north mean 10 percent of plantings in maturation phase, due to be harvested in mid-January.
MATO GROSSO DO SUL - good climate helped counterbalance lower plantings due to credit problems.
SAO PAULO - plantings rose only 3.6 percent from last year due to financing problems. Good rains in Mogiana region last week restored soil humidity to normal levels.
